stamps.label: Did You Hear What He Said?

lesson.menu_desc: A party, three strangers, and how small talk turns into a real conversation -- 13 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Breaking the Ice
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eglis Roberto | Lesson 3 -- Breaking the Ice

listenings.text: I hate small talk. You go to a party, and somebody asks you: so, what do you do? Where are you from? Nice weather, right? Ten minutes later, you know nothing about that person. I would rather ask a real question. Last week I was at a dinner, and I asked the woman next to me: what is something you have changed your mind about? She looked at me, surprised. Then she talked for twenty minutes. Now she is a good friend. So my advice is simple. Skip the weather. Ask something that matters, and the other person will remember you.

I do not agree with that. Small talk is not fake. Small talk is the door. You cannot walk into a stranger's life with a big question. People need a few easy minutes to feel safe. So I always start small. How do you know the host? Have you tried the food? Then I listen for one little detail: a place, a hobby, a trip. And I follow it. Oh, you sail? Really? Where do you sail? That is how the real conversation starts. Big questions are great, but only after the door is open.
